A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the outcome auditing process has helped to improve our service and has provided us with a framework for ongoing service development.

we have developed a set of measures that can be used by CAMHS teams in their routine clinical practice to audit the quality of care they provide and that these measures are valid, reliable and responsive to change in a variety of settings.

we have demonstrated the feasibility and acceptability of a user satisfaction survey and a clinician rated measure of change in symptoms and impairment in a large specialist child and adolescent service in the UK.

it is possible to develop and implement a comprehensive system for outcome auditing of CAMHS, which can be used to inform service development, to provide a measure of service accountability and to contribute to clinical governance.
